messages:
maya: thinking about a lightweight prefetch / soft-SLA shim for routing decisions. goal: reduce p99 for warm tenants without overprovisioning.
rohan: curious — is this KV-prefetch (kv cache warm) or pre-launching model instances?
sasha: both are valid levers. my rough idea: a two-tier prefetch: 1) prefix/KV warm for hot tenants, 2) speculative slot spinup for bursty traffic within tenant budget.
alex: important to quantify waste: prefetch work that never serves is pure cost. need metrics: prefetch_attempts, prefetch_hits, prefetch_waste_tokens, slot_spinup_success_rate.
maya: agree. also want a soft-SLA flag on route policy so router can opt into 'best-effort warm' vs 'no-warm' for strict cost controls. example policy snippet:```json
{"route": "tenant-*.prod", "soft_sla": true, "prefetch_budget_tokens": 2000, "spinup_timeout_ms": 150}
```
rohan: nice. how to encode budget enforcement? token budget per-minute? or sliding-window?
sasha: sliding-window works better for burst smoothing. propose: window=60s, max_prefetch_tokens=budget, replenish_rate=budget/60.
alex: eviction/credit transfer question: if tenant doesn't use prefetch tokens, should we allow short-term borrowing across tenants in same org? security/ISV concerns.
maya: prefer no cross-tenant borrowing by default. maybe allow org-level pooling behind explicit flag.
ops-bot: telemetry: created metric prefetch.job.started (tags: tenant, region), prefetch.job.evicted, prefetch.job.served.
rohan: what about region affinity? prefetching in a remote region can waste cross-region egress. router needs region penalty to avoid prefetching remote unless win > cost.
sasha: propose region_penalty = estimated_egress_cost + extra_latency_cost, normalized to token-equivalent units so policy can compare with prefetch benefit.
alex: rolling back if waste spikes: autoscaler should detect prefetch_waste_rate > 0.8 and disable soft_sla for that tenant automatically. quick kill switch.
maya: operational playbook: 1) start with conservative budget (500 tokens/min), 2) watch prefetch_hit_rate > 0.6 and p99 drop, 3) escalate budget or enable speculative spinup.
rohan: deployment plan: implement router-side flag + telemetry in one release, then a separate controller to manage budgets/auto-tuning. keeps rollback surface small.
sasha: interface boundary question: should controller live in policy engine or as a separate autoscaler service? I vote separate microservice that talks to policy engine via typed API (PATCH /route/{id}/soft_sla).
alex: separate service makes testing easier and keeps policy engine simpler. but add authenticated calls and rate limits.
maya: follow-ups: +1 to separate controller. @sasha can you draft small API and chart of metrics? @alex can you sketch rollback hooks? rohan, can you prototype client-side region_penalty estimator?
sasha: yep will send a draft in #architecture tomorrow.
alex: I'll add rollback hooks to the router: feature flag + runtime kill switch endpoint.
rohan: I'll prototype estimator and run a quick sim against existing traffic traces.
maya: thanks. quick note: let's also add a tenant opt-out so customers can disable warm behavior via account settings. compliance asks have come up.
sasha: good call. include opt-out in policy schema and expose via billing API.
ops-bot: action created: A-2743 prefetch-controller API draft assigned to sasha, due 1712544000.
maya: closing — solid plan. small experiment first, metrics gate before any scaling of budget. :thumbsup:
